chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He was asked about a man who performs Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj) and does not have a sacrificial animal (hady), so he fasts three days during Hajj, then dies after returning to his family before fasting the seven days. Is it upon his guardian to fulfill it on his behalf? He said: 'I do not see that he is obligated to fulfill it.'
ai.seo_question: Does a deceased pilgrim's family need to make up their incomplete Hajj fasts?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that if a pilgrim performing Tamattu' who could not afford a sacrificial animal fasts three days during Hajj and then dies before completing the remaining seven days, his guardian is not obligated to make up the remaining fasts on his behalf. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the expiation (Kaffarah) for Tamattu' is satisfied by the total of ten days, and death before completion does not impose a debt of fasting on the heir, distinguishing it from other obligatory acts like prayer.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having been asked about a man performing Tumatto with the Umra to the Hajj, and does not happen to have a sacrificial animal with him So he Fasts the three days during the Hajj, then dies after having returned to his family, before he Fasts the seven days. Is it upon his guardian that he fulfils it on his behalf?’ Heasws said: ‘Iasws do not see a repayment to be upon him’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man for al-Hajj al-Tamattu‘ (advantageous) who did not have an animal for offering. Therefore, he fasted for three days in al-Hajj : then he died after returning to his family and before fasting the seven days: if it was obligatory on his guardian to fast on his behalf. He (the Imam) said, ‘I do not see any Qada’ (compensatory fast) obligatory on him.’”
